newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Yakovlev still wants Fokker.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Yakovlev still wants Fokker.

text.p: Russian plane-maker Yakovlev is still optimistic it can buy bankrupt Dutch plane manufacturer Fokker NV, a senior company official said on Friday.

"We need to buy it (Fokker) because our main task is to secure 25-30 percent of the (Russian) short-range plane market by 2000," Alexander Dondukov, chief designer at Aviatsionnaya Korporatsiya Yakovlev, told Reuters.
Dondukov said that the deal could cost $200-270 million and that Yakovlev had asked the Russian government for financial guarantees for the deal.
"If the government does not give us guarantees, we are working out three reserve options of our own to close this deal sussesfully," he said, without elaborating.
Russian Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin said in October that Yakovlev was close to securing a Russian government credit line.
But Yakovlev is short of cash.

Moscow telephone company MGTS this month cut off almost all telephones at its headquarters because of an outstanding bill. Dondukov said the firm had paid its bills and all phones were working. "Now we want to finish this deal," he said.

Aviatsionnaya Korporatsiya Yakovlev used to be the Soviet Union's foremost designer of military aircraft and still designs naval fighter planes. It also designs passenger aircraft and produced the short-range Yak-40 and Yak-42 models.
South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries said earlier this month its bid for Fokker was also still active.
